label: verify-q1-literature

claims.claim: In K562 (1,000 x 1,000 design) most enhancers scale all promoters by similar fold-changes; multiplicative model R2=0.82; rank order largely preserved.
claims.source_says: most enhancers activated all promoters by similar amounts, and intrinsic enhancer and promoter activities combine multiplicatively to determine RNA output (R2=0.82). ... average Spearman correlation across all pairs of promoters = 0.81
claims.note: R2 and similar fold-change are stated; 'rank order preserved' is a fair reading of the Spearman 0.81.

claims.claim: In Drosophila 72% of 11,364 enhancers prefer one of two core promoters by at least 2-fold (housekeeping vs developmental).
claims.source_says: of the 11,364 enhancers, 8,144 (72%) activated one core promoter at least 2-fold more strongly than the other
claims.note: Exact match in the Zabidi 2015 full text; 'clearest rank-order change' is the agent's framing, not the paper's.

claims.claim: A structured minority deviates in the human data (E1/P1 1.93-fold), and the same K562 data show selectivity beyond noise by another group's test (90.46% of cCREs).
claims.source_says: for the majority of cCREs (90.46% at 0.1% FDR cutoff) the variance of boost indices was significantly larger than could be explained by experimental noise
claims.note: 90.46% is in the cited Martinez-Ara page; the 1.93-fold (P=4.19e-08) is in the Bergman page, not the cited one, but is correct there.

claims.claim: Promoter strength rescales enhancer input non-linearly (weak promoters boosted most; saturation at strong promoters and strongest enhancers), a mechanism that can reorder enhancers across promoters.
claims.source_says: these promoters scale the enhancer signals in a non-linear manner that depends on promoter strength. ... The apparent saturation observable at high enhancer activities in Figure 3C
claims.note: Cited 2024 paper supports non-linear scaling and saturation at high enhancer activity; 'weak promoters boosted most' and promoter saturation come from the 2022 paper, and 'can reorder enhancers' is the agent's inference.

overall: Three of four key claims check out against the original papers. The fourth is partly supported: it merges the 2022 and 2024 Martinez-Ara findings and adds an inference about reordering that no source states.
